items.title: Conflicting evidence on early mobilisation and stay
items.whyItMatters: A trial in selected patients and an adjusted registry analysis disagree (claim c3), so neither answers the question for this unit's patients.
items.opportunity: Estimate the association in the unit's own patients with a pre-specified adjustment strategy.

items.title: Confounding by indication
items.whyItMatters: The reasons for delay also predict long stays (claim c4).
items.opportunity: Adjust for pre-surgical characteristics, report estimates with and without postoperative conditions, and check the weekend-delay subgroup.

items.title: Reading every patient's notes is unaffordable
items.whyItMatters: About 1,260 patients over three years at 25 minutes each would take over 500 hours against 100 available.
items.opportunity: Sample cases with long stays and two controls per case.

items.title: Patients with dementia are missing from the trial evidence
items.whyItMatters: Trials excluded many patients with dementia or delirium, who make up a large share of the unit's patients.
items.opportunity: Report the association separately for patients with dementia.

errorsFound: Reading the trial result as proof for this unit ignores that it excluded about 30 percent of screened patients.
reevaluation: The gaps confirm the case-control design with a pre-specified adjustment strategy and a dementia subgroup.
summary: Four gaps; the conflicting evidence and confounding by indication are high severity.
